records.title: DCO: Dynamic Cache Orchestration for LLM Accelerators through Predictive Management
records.reason: The abstract proposes predictive cache replacement, bypass, and thrash mitigation on a shared cache for LLM accelerators, directly addressing runtime memory hierarchy behavior.

records.title: Enhancing memory retrieval in generative agents through LLM-trained cross attention networks
records.reason: The title describes memory retrieval for generative agents using cross-attention networks, but does not establish a systems-efficiency contribution. The official Frontiers URL returned an access error and no primary abstract was retrieved; retain as borderline pending the primary abstract.

records.title: Accelerating Large Language Model Training with Hybrid GPU-based Compression
records.reason: The abstract explicitly targets LLM training through hybrid GPU compression; training-only acceleration is outside the inference-focused scope.

records.title: Task-agnostic Distillation of Encoder-Decoder Language Models
records.reason: The primary abstract explicitly describes task-agnostic, compute-efficient, performance-preserving encoder-decoder language models through distillation. It does not report serving measurements, but smaller compute-efficient language models are a plausible inference-efficiency lineage candidate; retain for later Research screening.

records.title: BitHydra: Towards Bit-flip Inference Cost Attack against Large Language Models
records.reason: The abstract frames bit-flip methods as an inference-cost attack against LLMs; it studies an attack/threat rather than a system technique that improves inference efficiency.

records.title: EdgeMM: Multi-Core CPU with Heterogeneous AI-Extension and Activation-aware Weight Pruning for Multimodal LLMs at Edge
records.reason: The abstract combines a multi-core edge CPU, heterogeneous AI extensions, and activation-aware weight pruning specifically for multimodal LLM inference, directly targeting constrained edge execution.

records.title: QWHA: Quantization-Aware Walsh-Hadamard Adaptation for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning on Large Language Models
records.reason: The primary abstract states that quantization reduces LLM inference cost and presents quantization-aware PEFT to produce accurate, efficient quantized models. Its method includes fine-tuning, but the stated deployment/inference-efficiency connection is explicit, so retain for later Research screening.

records.title: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts LLMs for Efficient ICD Code Prediction in Clinical Outcome Modeling
records.reason: The title describes sparse MoE models for efficient clinical-code prediction, a domain-specific task that may use model sparsity but does not establish a reusable LLM serving technique. The primary DOI route was inaccessible and the abstract was not retrieved; retain as borderline pending the primary abstract.

records.title: GWT: Scalable Optimizer State Compression for Large Language Model Training
records.reason: GWT compresses optimizer state for large language model training, an explicitly training-only efficiency target.

records.title: Multiscale Aggregated Hierarchical Attention (MAHA): A Game Theoretic and Optimization Driven Approach to Efficient Contextual Modeling in Large Language Models
records.reason: The primary abstract identifies quadratic self-attention cost as a bottleneck for long-context LLMs and proposes hierarchical attention for efficient contextual modeling. The architecture-level inference-efficiency connection is plausible even though serving measurements are not established in the abstract; retain for later Research screening.

records.title: FPMoE: A Sparse Mixture-of-Experts Approach to Functional Code Generation
records.reason: The primary abstract proposes a sparse MoE for functional-language code generation and reports matching larger code models with only 3B active parameters. This is a plausible sparse-model inference-efficiency candidate; retain for later Research screening despite the domain-specific task and abstract-level evidence.

records.title: Co-LMLM: Continuous-Query Limited Memory Language Models
records.reason: The abstract proposes a continuous-query limited-memory language model, directly addressing bounded context/memory during repeated language-model inference.

records.title: MoEC: A Memory-Routed Mixture-of-Experts Controller for Adaptive Minecraft Control
records.reason: The title describes a memory-routed MoE controller for Minecraft agents, a task-specific application with no stated serving-efficiency goal. The ACL Anthology PDF returned HTTP 503 and no primary abstract was retrieved; retain as borderline pending the primary abstract.

records.reason: The title describes LoRA fine-tuning for tiny language models under constrained deployment but does not establish an inference-time systems-efficiency contribution. records.title: CoT-UQ: Improving Response-wise Uncertainty Quantification in LLMs with Chain-of-Thought
records.reason: CoT-UQ targets response-wise uncertainty quantification using chain-of-thought, an output reliability objective rather than inference-system efficiency.

records.title: Prune 'n Predict: Optimizing LLM Decision-making with Conformal Prediction
records.reason: The paper title suggests pruning LLM decisions with conformal prediction, but the available abstract evidence does not establish reduced model execution, token generation, or serving resources.

records.title: QUASAR: Quantum Assembly Code Generation Using Tool-Augmented LLMs via Agentic RL
records.reason: The paper applies tool-augmented LLMs and agentic reinforcement learning to quantum assembly-code generation; quantum compilation is the application, not an LLM inference efficiency method.

records.title: Enhancing chest X-ray datasets with privacy-preserving large language models and multi-type annotations: a data-driven approach for improved classification
records.reason: The paper uses LLMs to create annotated chest X-ray data for downstream classification; this is a medical data/application workflow, not inference systems efficiency.

records.title: PRvL: Quantifying the Capabilities and Risks of Large Language Models for PII Redaction
records.reason: The paper evaluates LLM capability and risk for PII redaction, an application/safety assessment without a concrete inference execution optimization.

records.title: Lossless Compression of Large Language Model-Generated Text via Next-Token Prediction
records.reason: The title and abstract describe lossless compression of generated text using next-token prediction; this may reduce output storage/transmission, but does not establish lower LLM inference cost or serving resource use.
